### Cardiac Hypertrophy

Pressure overload produces concentric hypertrophy; volume overload produces eccentric hypertrophy. Histologically: increased myocyte diameter, boxcar nuclei, and interstitial fibrosis.

### Myocardial Infarction - Time Course

0-4h: wavy fibers only. 4-24h: coagulative necrosis begins, early neutrophils. 1-3 days: dense neutrophilic infiltration, contraction band necrosis, highest rupture risk at 3-7 days. 1-3 weeks: granulation tissue with capillaries and fibroblasts. Weeks-months: mature fibrous scar with compensatory hypertrophy.

### Valvular Disease

Acute Rheumatic Fever: Aschoff bodies with Anitschkow cells and fibrinoid necrosis. Small verrucous vegetations. Chronic RHD: valve thickening, commissural fusion, fish-mouth stenosis. Infective Endocarditis: large irregular vegetations with bacterial colonies and valve destruction.

### Myocarditis

Lymphocytic infiltration with myocyte necrosis (most commonly viral, Coxsackievirus B). Giant cell myocarditis has a fulminant course.

### Cardiomyopathies

Dilated: four-chamber dilation with interstitial fibrosis. Hypertrophic: asymmetric septal hypertrophy with myocyte disarray. Restrictive: impaired diastolic filling from endomyocardial fibrosis or infiltrative disease. ARVC: fibrofatty replacement of right ventricular myocardium.

### Cardiac Tumors

Myxoma: most common primary cardiac tumor, stellate cells in myxoid stroma. Rhabdomyoma: spider cells with glycogen-laden vacuolated cytoplasm, associated with tuberous sclerosis.
